claim_ceiling: Historical trust-model analysis/estimated exposure is not proof of contemporary exploitable package-manager vulnerabilities or benign package behavior
source_basis: Author published PDF pp. 2, 9: Sections 2.1-2.4, selected trace-estimation discussion and 9

title: Towards Measuring Supply Chain Attacks on Package Managers for Interpreted Languages
evidence_object: Registry feature comparison and suspicious-package findings from metadata/static/dynamic vetting
claim_ceiling: A discovery/measurement study documents found cases, not high coverage, evasion resistance or a benign verdict for unflagged packages
source_basis: Published NDSS PDF pp. 4, 8, 13: Sections III-A, selected III-B4/IV and V-B

title: Backstabber's Knife Collection: A Review of Open Source Software Supply Chain Attacks
evidence_object: Observed/previously described package-attack trees and manually analyzed obtainable malicious-package subset
claim_ceiling: Selected known/obtainable cases cannot establish attack prevalence, complete taxonomy or coverage of safeguards
source_basis: Author arXiv v1 PDF pp. 4, 9, 18: Sections 3, selected 4.3/5 and 6.2-6.3

title: Small World with High Risks: A Study of Security Threats in the npm Ecosystem
evidence_object: Historical npm dependency/maintainer graph reach and public-advisory vulnerability reach
claim_ceiling: Dependency/maintainer reach is potential impact, not observed exploitation, authenticated author identity or contemporary risk prevalence
source_basis: Author published PDF pp. 4-5, 10, 13: Sections 3.1-3.2, selected 4.3 and 6

title: What Are Weak Links in the npm Supply Chain?
evidence_object: Six proposed risk signals from npm package metadata and practitioner perceptions
claim_ceiling: Perceived weak-link indicators are not calibrated attack probabilities, complete mitigations or malicious-package labels
source_basis: Author published PDF pp. 3, 8-9: Sections 3.1, selected 3.2.1, survey agreement/new signals and 6-7

title: Le-git-imate: Towards Verifiable Web-Based Git Repositories
evidence_object: User-intent verification records bound to Git commit tree, parents, author fields and merge strategy
claim_ceiling: Commit-content and recorded-intent binding depends on trusted keys, local verification and manual UI checks; not real-human identity, licensing or safe-code certification
source_basis: Author published PDF pp. 7-9, 13: Section 5.4, selected Section 6, Appendix A/B background and C Verify_Commits algorithm

title: Contour: A Practical System for Binary Transparency
evidence_object: Binary commitments/inclusion proofs anchored to a consensus log, with monitors and optional archival nodes
claim_ceiling: Binary transparency proves logged commitment under consensus assumptions, not benign source, behavior or availability of unmirrored data
source_basis: Author arXiv v2 PDF pp. 1, 3, 6-7, 11: Sections 3.1, 5.5, 6.1-6.3 and 8.3-8.5 (selected)

title: Text2App: A Framework for Creating Android Apps from Text Descriptions
evidence_object: Natural-language descriptions, SAR tokens, template-generated .scm/.bky files and App Inventor APKs
claim_ceiling: feasibility of an AI-mediated Android creation transformation
source_basis: arXiv PDF pp. 2-6, 9-10: Sections 3.1-3.7, 4-5; Figure 2; Appendices A-D; selected full-text recheck; no cover-to-cover claim

title: AppForge: From Assistant to Independent Developer---Are GPTs Ready for Software Development?
evidence_object: 101 Android development specifications, generated project files, APKs, UI tests and crash tests
claim_ceiling: AI-mediated multi-step artifact creation context
source_basis: arXiv v1 PDF pp. 4-7, 9, 18-19: Sections 3.1-3.4, 4.1-4.3; Appendices B.3-B.6; selected full-text recheck; no cover-to-cover claim

title: Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot's Code Contributions
evidence_object: Copilot technical-preview completions for scenario-specific software/hardware CWEs
claim_ceiling: Non-vulnerable for one target CWE is not globally secure or functionally correct; prompt-context selection is proprietary and model outputs nonreproducible
source_basis: arXiv PDF pp. 3, 5, 13: Sections II-III, IV-D, V-A1/V-B1, VI and Threats to Validity

title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
evidence_object: Human final responses and assistant interactions on five analyzed security tasks
claim_ceiling: Task-specific final-code security differs from functional correctness and from trust/self-reported confidence; assistant influence is not equal to direct copying

title: Lost at C: A User Study on the Security Implications of Large Language Model Code Assistants
evidence_object: 58 student programmers' C shopping-list submissions and captured assistant interactions
claim_ceiling: L6 task-specific security observations; no general assistant-safety or lineage guarantee
source_basis: USENIX PDF pp. 5-6, 8-11, 14 (printed pp. 2208-2209, 2211-2214, 2217): Sections 3, 4.3 and 5.2; selected full-text recheck; no cover-to-cover claim

title: We Have a Package for You! A Comprehensive Analysis of Package Hallucinations by Code Generating LLMs
evidence_object: Package recommendations extracted from Python/JavaScript generation and follow-up prompts
claim_ceiling: dependency-recommendation risk evidence
source_basis: USENIX PDF pp. 5-8, 13-14 (printed pp. 3690-3693, 3698-3699): Sections 3-4, 5.1, 6-7; selected full-text recheck; no cover-to-cover claim

title: How Secure Is Code Generated by ChatGPT?
evidence_object: 21 small generated programs across five languages and security-targeted correction dialogues
claim_ceiling: A targeted correction or plausible security explanation is not global program security, functional correctness or a reliable general repair strategy
source_basis: arXiv PDF pp. 2, 5-6: Dataset Description; selected Security Analysis; Sections IV-V

title: CodexLeaks: Privacy Leaks from Code Generation Language Models in GitHub Copilot
evidence_object: Generated responses, public-source association and human-confirmed privacy exposure in a historical Codex study
claim_ceiling: A public-source match is evidence of association, not an exact training-membership certificate or an authenticated derivation edge

title: Android App Repackaging Detection: A Comprehensive Survey
evidence_object: Survey taxonomy of structural/token/semantic, API, resource and TPL detection representations
claim_ceiling: Selected primary survey sections establish topical coverage, not an all-dimensional synthesis or correctness of every secondary method description
source_basis: Publisher HTML Sections 1 (Introduction), 4.1 (Code fingerprint-based detection), 4.3 (API-based detection), 4.5 (Third-party library-based detection)

title: A Survey of Third-Party Library Security Research in Application Software
evidence_object: Cross-platform TPL security review separating known-library matching and unsupervised discovery
claim_ceiling: secondary synthesis of TPL security research
source_basis: arXiv v1 PDF pp. 3, 7-10, 16-17: framework; Sections 3.1-3.2 and 5.1-5.2; selected full-text recheck; no cover-to-cover claim

title: Software Supply Chain Security: A Systematic Literature Review
evidence_object: review taxonomy, protocol, or cross-cutting framework
claim_ceiling: cross-cutting
source_basis: publisher/arXiv abstract, selected passages where accessible, and bibliographic record; no exhaustive full-text claim

title: Research Directions in Software Supply Chain Security
evidence_object: Dependencies, build infrastructure, humans, SBOM/VEX and LLM-mediated development
claim_ceiling: Visibility/provenance does not alone capture unconventional injection or establish reachability/exploitability; self-declared VEX requires trustworthy evidence

title: Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management: From Threats to Treatment
evidence_object: Supplier-type cyber supply-chain risk governance, standards and organizational controls
claim_ceiling: Contractual/security-process compliance and SBOM guidance do not attest one APK or establish its behavioral security
source_basis: Publisher PDF pp. 2, 6-7, 9: Section 1 methodology, Sections 3.1-3.3, Table 2, Table 3 and Section 4 discussion

title: Software Supply Chain: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Mitigations and Risk Assessment Strategies
evidence_object: review taxonomy, protocol, or cross-cutting framework
claim_ceiling: cross-cutting
source_basis: selected full-text sections plus bibliographic record; exact reading boundary retained in source_locations.csv

title: On the Way to SBOMs: Investigating Design Issues and Solutions in Practice
evidence_object: SBOM-related GitHub issue discussions and reported design issues/solutions
claim_ceiling: Discussion-derived themes and proposed solutions do not demonstrate complete SBOMs, exploitability or authenticated build lineage
source_basis: arXiv v2 PDF pp. 6, 12, 21: Sections 3.3.1, 4.2.1, 6 and selected 7

title: BOMs Away! Inside the Minds of Stakeholders: A Comprehensive Study of Bills of Materials for Software Systems
evidence_object: Stakeholder perceptions about SBOM/HBOM/AIBOM/DataBOM production, consumption and verification
claim_ceiling: Dependency-vulnerability presence is not product impact; SBOM integrity in transit and correctness/completeness of its content need different checks
source_basis: Author published PDF pp. 3-4, 7-8, 10-11: Sections 3-3.2, 4.2 C1-C11 (selected), Table 5, Section 5 and 6
